Material S1 Determination method of substitution degree and reaction efficiency of modified lignosulfonic acid S1 Table S1 Cumulative release of EB-SL conjugate and EB-SC in 50% methanol-water S2 Table S2 Cumulative release of EB-SL conjugate and BE-SC in soil S2 Material S1 Determination method of substitution degree and reaction efficiency of modified lignosulfonic acid [1] The amount of the sulfonic acid group substitution on the sodium lignosulfonate unit is expressed by the degree of substitution (DS). Accurately weigh 0.300 g of dry modified lignosulfonic acid into a 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask, add 25 mL of 0.100 M NaOH, ultrasonically dissolve it and stir for 1 h to make it fully react. Then phenolphthalein is used as an indicator to titrate the excess NaOH with 0.100 M hydrochloric acid until the brick red just disappears. The volume of HCl consumed was recorded as V1, and the average of three parallel titrations was taken. At the same time, the same operation was performed with unmodified sodium lignosulfonate, and the volume of HCl consumed was recorded as V2. The actual degree of substitution (DS) was calculated according to formulas (1) and (2). 1) The DS calculation formula is as follows:
